name: Resume — dagmar wayfinder (2026-07-31)
description: Resume — dagmar wayfinder (2026-07-31, updated 2026-08-01). Foundation + Autonomy DECIDED; doc set passed foundations + schaue + 2026-08-01 review and is consistent + self-contained -- do not re-litigate. Domain model in CONTEXT.md (Tier A Dagger / B os-eco ports / C dagmar; CRD set {Project,Agent,Prompt,QualityGate,Trigger,Run}); ADRs 0001-0009 in docs/adr/ (0001 layered language, 0002 CRD boundary, 0003 in-repo ProjectManifest .dagmar/project.yaml, 0004 Hybrid-C topology, 0005 canopy Variant-A cross-store prompt composition, 0006 autonomy model - slim axes, deterministic merge, two-green+veto, Calibration Agent, 0007 credentials - per-Project MANDATORY namespace + typed secrets + ESO + projected injection, two-layer defense (namespace + Sandbox encapsulation), 0008 engine tenancy - singleton engine, kube-pod agent pods + pods/exec RBAC, per-Project cache volumes, 0009 quality-gate workflow family - deterministic Justfile gate dagmar-bootstrap/dagmar-gate, hermetic LLM via tool-set, gate-before-review + revise loop + max-N, Calibration loop on disagreement, one ReviewAgent, delivery auto-merge/human-PR-handoff, post-merge watchdog filtered safety-net). dagmar framed as Dagger-based SOFTWARE FACTORY (Workflow-CRD framework spun out). Research on main: canopy-prompt-model + dagger-in-k8s + spike-engine-tenancy (Q3 validated in kind). CLOSED: dagmar-4271, 8097, fa45, 4c9f (ADR-0007), cbb8 (ADR-0008), e95b (ADR-0009). OPEN seeds: dagmar-ff60 (Workflow-CRD framework), dagmar-911b (Sandbox trust-zones/hermetic-LLM, security, sharpens ADR-0007), dagmar-1775 (Destination software-factory), dagmar-d8f0 (cache-volume-name validation pre-auto-merge), dagmar-3684 (Go module layout/hex arch), dagmar-e795 (self-bootstrap). Next recommended: dagmar-3684 (Go module layout) or dagmar-911b (Sandbox trust-zones). Reminders: DE chat / EN persisted writing; CLIs sd/ml/cn; gh=denkhaus; git author denkhaus@github.local; agent subprocesses need worktree isolation; canopy v0.2.6 native. dagmar Dagger module under .dagger/ (source=.dagger, own go.mod dagger/dagmar); DO NOT delete .dagger generated files (dagger.gen.go, internal/dagger) - git-ignored but required for main.go to compile, regenerate via dagger develop.

name: dagmar domain model (CONTEXT.md)
description: dagmar's ubiquitous language is pinned in CONTEXT.md (repo root) + ADRs 0001-0003 (docs/adr/). Tier model: A=Dagger (reused by reference), B=os-eco (adapter ports, bound per-Project), C=dagmar (coin terms ONLY here). CRD set {Project, Agent, Prompt, QualityGate, Trigger, Run}; non-CR {Task=seeds issue, Sandbox->Pod, Workspace->clone}; ProjectManifest = in-repo per-Project conformance contract (checkables+os-eco+prompt-JSON+flow), NOT a CRD. Gating spine: QualityGate composes checkables + ReviewAgent (an Agent role) + merge rules. Plan deferred (seeds concept; future Telegram Plan-Agent idea in references). Authoritative for dagmar-4271.

title: ADR-0007: Credentials & secret management
rationale: Closes foundations-review C2 / seed dagmar-4c9f. Per-Project K8s namespace = trust boundary; 3 typed secret classes (vcs/os-eco/llm) as native Secrets; External Secrets Operator = source-of-truth with native Secret as runtime contract (baseline pre-ESO: controller-managed); encryption-at-rest required; injection Project->Sandbox->dag.Env() least-privilege per-Run; merge stays controller-level (ADR-0006), secrets never in prompts (ADR-0005). Deferred to impl: RBAC/SA-per-Project, short-lived tokens, rotation cadence, ESO backend.

name: Hermetic k3s-in-Dagger bringup (cbb8 spike)
description: Proven recipe to bring up an isolated k3s cluster inside the Dagger engine (dogfood path for dagmar). k := dag.K3S(cluster); k.Server().Start(ctx); then a GO-LEVEL retry loop calling k.Kubectl(get nodes -o wide).Stdout(ctx) until err==nil with a 3s sleep, because k3s writes the kubeconfig before the API serves (readiness race). Returns the node table. Validated on Docker Desktop/WSL2: k3s v1.34.1, nested privileges/cgroup v2 OK, 10-16s cold start. Anti-patterns in the failure record.

Passing shell-loop args to the k3s Kubectl() helper (e.g. k.Kubectl(get nodes ... && exit 0 || loop).Stdout(ctx)) returns an EMPTY string with NO error even though kubectl succeeded — the helper runs sh -c (kubectl + args) and complex control flow breaks .Stdout capture. (Earlier also claimed direct alpine/kubectl containers could not reach the API — DISPROVED by mx-b8452d: alpine/helm reaches the k3s API fine; that earlier failure was the non-existent alpine/kubectl:1.34 image tag, not connectivity.)
resolution: Use the k3s module Kubectl() helper with SIMPLE args (no shell loop), wrapped in a GO-LEVEL retry for API readiness. Direct alpine/helm + k.Config() containers DO reach the k3s API (validated, mx-b8452d) — just use valid image tags.

name: Deploy Dagger engine nested in k3s-in-Dagger (cbb8 — nesting VALIDATED)
description: Recipe: k:=dag.K3S(cluster); k.Server().Start(ctx); waitForAPI (Go-retry of k.Kubectl get nodes, because k3s writes kubeconfig before the API serves); then an alpine/helm:3.14.0 container with k.Config() runs: helm upgrade --install --create-namespace -n dagmar --set image.tag=v0.21.8 --set privileged=true --wait --timeout 5m dagger oci://registry.dagger.io/dagger-helm; then EXPLICIT kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod -l name=dagger-dagger-helm-engine (helm --wait on a DaemonSet returns BEFORE the pod is fully Ready). RESULT validated 2026-08-01 on Docker Desktop/WSL2: engine pod 1/1 Running Ready, 0 restarts, age ~3m — a Dagger engine runs nested (privileged DaemonSet in k3s in Dagger). Confirms Hybrid-C in-cluster engine feasibility for ADR-0008. IMPORTANT correction: the alpine/helm direct container reached the k3s API fine, so the earlier failure record claim that direct containers cannot reach the API was WRONG — that earlier failure was the bad alpine/kubectl:1.34 image tag, not connectivity.

title: cbb8 tenancy direction: singleton engine + per-project cache isolation
rationale: User direction (2026-08-01): a SINGLE Dagger engine serves all Projects (one engine pod, one shared hostPath cache store — observed in the dagger-helm DaemonSet manifest at /var/lib/dagger-* and /run/dagger-*). Cross-Project CACHE isolation is achieved by per-project CACHE VOLUME NAMES (Dagger isolates cache by volume name), not by per-project namespaces. Namespaces are optional (defense-in-depth: blast-radius, NetworkPolicy, ResourceQuota); user stays open to multi-namespace IF it brings a decisive advantage, using a common prefix dagmar-<project> for traceability. Credential-to-LLM isolation is a Sandbox/encapsulation property (tokens injected transiently by controller/engine, never in the LLM-reachable env), NOT a namespace property — this sharpens ADR-0007 rationale without changing its storage/scoping decision. Still to validate empirically: (a) singleton engine serves a client via kube-pod:// (Research Q3), (b) cache isolation by volume name (Q1).

description: cbb8 spike: the nested Dagger engine (privileged DaemonSet, registry.dagger.io/engine:v0.21.8, via helm oci://registry.dagger.io/dagger-helm, in k3s-in-Docker-Desktop/WSL2) does NOT reliably reach Ready. helm install always succeeds, but the engine pod rollout/Ready condition TIMES OUT (kubectl rollout status --timeout=300s) on most attempts; observed 1/1 Running Ready (0 restarts) exactly once (spike-eng5). k3s itself is reliable; the engine pod is the bottleneck. Likely causes (unconfirmed): engine image pull latency into a fresh k3s per cluster name, privileged-engine boot under triple nesting, or resource pressure on the single nested node.
resolution: Unresolved. Engine-pod readiness reliability must be fixed before the kube-pod:// multi-client (Q3) and cache-isolation (Q1) experiments can run. Candidate fixes: (1) persistent k3s cluster via dagger service up so the engine image is pulled ONCE and reused across runs (the dominant cost is the fresh pull per dagger call); (2) resource/timeout tuning; (3) accept that the spike host (Docker Desktop) differs from production (dedicated runner nodes per ADR-0004) and that prod may not have this problem. Singleton-engine tenancy decision is unaffected.

name: Dagger image cache for nested k3s via KeepState
description: The marcosnils/k3s module wipes /var/lib/rancher/k3s (incl. the containerd image store) on each start by default (keepState=false), so the ~500MB engine image is RE-PULLED every dagger call. Fix: dag.K3S(name, dagger.K3SOpts{KeepState: true}) + a STABLE cluster name across calls -> the Dagger cache volume (k3s_cache_<name>) persists containerd images -> engine image pulled ONCE. Measured 2026-08-01: cold deploy 11.5min, warm/cached deploy 17s. This is Dagger image-cache strategy for nested clusters (cache volumes as persistence). Answer to the owner question.

cbb8 spike: k3s flannel CNI is flaky in the nested environment (k3s-in-Docker-in-Docker-Desktop/WSL2). Pod sandbox creation fails with: plugin type=flannel failed: loadFlannelSubnetEnv failed: open /run/flannel/subnet.env: no such file or directory. The engine pod then fails to get a network sandbox and kube-pod:// exec into it fails. INTERMITTENT: the engine pod reached 1/1 Ready once (spike-eng5) but fails on other runs. keepState=true may worsen it by resuming a stale flannel state. This is separate from the image-cache problem (which KeepState solves).
resolution: Unresolved in the marcosnils/k3s module. Options: (a) disable flannel (--flannel-backend=none) + alternate CNI in the k3s container; (b) pivot to kind for the spike (kindnetd CNI is reliable in Docker, kind cluster persists across dagger calls, kind load docker-image preloads from Docker cache); (c) accept k3s-in-dagger as feasible-but-flaky and consolidate. Recommendation: kind is the pragmatic spike environment; k3s-in-dagger feasibility (one Ready run) is recorded, and production (dedicated runner nodes, ADR-0004) likely avoids the nested-CNI issue.

name: Q3 validated: singleton Dagger engine serves a client pod via kube-pod://
description: Empirically validated 2026-08-01 in a kind cluster (the reliable spike environment, after k3s-in-dagger flannel flakiness). Setup: helm-installed the Dagger engine as a privileged DaemonSet (registry.dagger.io/engine:v0.21.8) in kind; a SEPARATE client pod (alpine + dagger CLI from the GitHub release tarball https://github.com/dagger/dagger/releases/download/v0.21.8/dagger_v0.21.8_linux_amd64.tar.gz + kubectl via apk, with a ServiceAccount dagger-client + Role/RoleBinding granting pods/exec) set _EXPERIMENTAL_DAGGER_RUNNER_HOST=kube-pod://<engine-pod>?namespace=dagmar, built an in-cluster kubeconfig from its SA token, and ran dagger core version. RESULT: connected to the singleton engine (client-version=v0.21.8, server-version=v0.21.8), returned v0.21.8, pod Succeeded. CONCLUSION (Research Q3): a singleton Dagger engine CAN serve a separate client/agent pod via kube-pod://, given the client has a ServiceAccount with pods/exec RBAC on the engine pod. This proves dagmar agent-pod-model feasibility. Manifest: /tmp/q3-client.yaml (SA+Role+RoleBinding+Pod). NOTE: dl.dagger.io install script returns 403 from the pod; use the GitHub release tarball instead. NOTE: the engine image (Wolfi) has dagger but no curl/wget/apk, so the client must be alpine-based.

title: A1 resolved: namespaces MANDATORY per Project + two-layer credential defense
rationale: Resolved the ADR-0007 vs ADR-0008 contradiction (2026-08-01 review item A1, security-critical). Decision: per-Project namespaces are MANDATORY (ADR-0007 wins - namespace = hard K8s-native credential boundary); ADR-0008 retracts its earlier namespaces-optional framing and reframes its tenancy/cache isolation (per-Project ServiceAccount/pods-exec RBAC + cache-volume names) as a layer ON TOP OF the mandatory namespace boundary, not instead-of. Defense in depth, two layers: (1) per-Project namespace boundary (strongest, native), (2) Sandbox encapsulation (secrets projected per-Run, never in the LLM-reachable environment). ADR-0007 and ADR-0008 amended with mutual cross-refs (review D1 also resolved). CONTEXT.md Engine glossary (A2) and ReviewAgent prompt (A3) reconciled.

title: ADR-0009 quality-gate workflow family
rationale: Decided via grilling 2026-08-01 (seed dagmar-e95b). Deterministic gate via project Justfile targets dagmar-bootstrap (net: install) + dagmar-gate (net: checkables+rules+static-analysis); hermetic LLM agent loop (no net, enforced via tool-set - no network tools); decision flow gate-before-review, both gate-red and veto are feedback, max N rounds then escalate; Calibration loop on disagreement (Gate-green AND Veto) emits review-calibration mixin -> co-evolve (ADR-0006, operator-approved initially); one ReviewAgent (specialists later); delivery auto=merge / human=PR-handoff; post-merge watchdog = separate filtered-trigger workflow (excludes dagmar own merges -> no loop), fix-PR on red/veto. Spun out: Workflow-CRD framework, Sandbox trust-zones (sharpens ADR-0007), Destination software-factory. Deferred: Calibration auto-apply, specialist reviewers, concurrency.

title: Gate timing reconciled: invariant pre-merge gate + separate post-merge watchdog (mache review A1)
rationale: Resolved 2026-08-01-mache review A1: CONTEXT.md L151, ADR-0006 L26, ADR-0009 §7/§8 described the authority=human gate timing three different ways. ADR-0009 (newest, most detailed) is authoritative: the gate is invariant and ALWAYS runs pre-merge on the candidate (advisory under authority=human); the post-merge behavior is a SEPARATE watchdog workflow with a filtered trigger, not 'the gate running post-merge'. Reconciled all three docs to that model and fixed ADR-0009's loose (ADR-0006) pre-merge citation. Also pinned manifest=what / dagmar-gate=how (B2), added Workflow glossary stub (B1), made hermeticity boundary depend explicitly on forthcoming trust-zone ADR (B3).

title: ADR-0010: Go module layout & hexagonal architecture
rationale: dagmar's Go skeleton lives in the .dagger module (dagger/dagmar) under .dagger/internal/{domain,ports,adapters,app,tools,workflows,config,log}; root github.com/denkhaus/dagmar deferred (future k8s control-plane). Functional core: Tier-A Dagger primitives used DIRECTLY in app/ (not ported; ADR-0001), only Tier-B os-eco gets ports, pure decisions in domain/ (0 Dagger import, unit-tested). Dagmar main object + New(project *dagger.Directory, seeds, mulch, canopy) constructor = per-Project binding seam for the kube-pod:// agent-pod client (ADR-0008). Testing: three-tier + GoMock (uber mockgen); DI plain constructors (no samber/do). Config/log/obs minimal-dep (slog, envconfig+ProjectManifest, Dagger otel, Langfuse deferred). v0 vertical Sandbox proven end-to-end. v0.21.8 constraints recorded in the ADR.

name: dagmar Go module skeleton (.dagger/internal)
description: Code lives in .dagger/ (module dagger/dagmar). .dagger/internal/: domain (pure functional core, 0 Dagger import, unit-tested); ports (Tier-B os-eco interfaces IssueTracker/Memory/Prompts/Tracer; mocks via ports/generate.go + go.uber.org/mock mockgen); adapters/{oseco,otel}; app (orchestration, Tier-A Dagger SDK via dagger.Connect() DIRECT, //go:build integration tests); tools + workflows (reusable composed units); config (envconfig + ProjectManifest ADR-0003); log (Logger interface + slog). main.go = Dagmar main object + New(project *dagger.Directory, seeds, mulch, canopy) constructor (per-Project binding seam) + Sandbox(image, workingDir) vertical returning *Sandbox. Build/test: GOWORK=off go -C .dagger build|test|vet. Regenerate after signature changes: dagger develop (NOT dagger generate). Root module github.com/denkhaus/dagmar empty (deferred control-plane). See docs/adr/0010-go-module-layout.md.

title: ADR-0011: Sandbox trust-zones — hermetic LLM via tailored tool-sets (calculated risk)
rationale: Closes seed dagmar-911b / resolves ADR-0009 §3's deferred per-tool boundary. ONE singleton engine (ADR-0008 unchanged, no re-open; the reviewed 'two-engines bell' was rejected — G1 image-resolution, G2 cross-engine handoff, G3 checkable split vs CONTEXT.md 'reused checkable', G4 DNS-exfil). Hermeticity of the LLM loop is enforced via per-use-case TAILORED TOOL-SETS (least privilege): hermetic agents (cognitive LLM-loop agents — coder, ReviewAgent; NOT deterministic bootstrap/gate) withhold the network-capable tools wholesale — http, git remote, and the ENTIRE container tool (container.WithExec() always has network per ProbeNet; no egress-free sub-lever). 'Hermetic' = tool-SURFACE constraint (no network tool on the Env), NOT a network air-gap. The ProbeNet residual (raw-exec/checkable path reaches network despite tool-set) is a CALCULATED, accepted risk: primary threat (LLM exfiltrating via its own tools) controlled by tool-set + per-Project llm key never in any tool-set; residual bound = ADR-0007 per-Project namespace + projected-secret subset; a malicious project-declared checkable compromises only its own namespace (gate runs but does not inspect). Out-of-scope residual NAMED: a Dagger Sandbox isolation break on the shared engine (the bell would have contained it) — accepted as a separate lower-probability residual, bounded by namespace. ProbeNet spike retained as residual-risk evidence. Reviewed 07 (bell, rejected) + 08 (accepted with N1-N6 sharpening).

name: Cache isolation by name validated (ADR-0008 Q1, local engine)
description: Empirically validated 2026-08-03 via the ProbeCache spike (.dagger/main.go, 3 separate 'dagger call probe-cache --mode {write|readsame|readdiff}' invocations = 3 client sessions against ONE engine): same cache-volume name SHARES the marker (positive control), a DIFFERENT name does NOT (ISOLATED). So Dagger isolates cache by volume NAME at the engine level — independent of whether clients are local processes or kube-pod:// clients. ADR-0008 §3's design assumption holds. The remaining cross-Project concern is therefore purely a control-plane guarantee: the controller must allocate DISTINCT cache-volume names per Project (already on ADR-0008's ops plate). Pre-condition for multi-Project mergeAuthority==auto is satisfied. In-cluster kind test available as Tier 2 but not strictly required — the engine-level mechanic is topology-agnostic.

title: ADR-0012: Self-bootstrap & dogfooding trajectory
rationale: Decided via grilling (seed dagmar-e795), revised per reviews 10+11. (1) Substrate: local kind cluster, CRDs real from the start, trajectory kind->real->triggers->in-cluster; root module gains api/v1alpha1/+controller. (2) Bootstrap boundary = dispatch vertical WITHOUT LLM (Project+Run-CR+controller reconciles a Run -> agent pod via kube-pod:// -> module call -> status back); Phase-0 reads (agent-pod image + module ref) are IN-scope, not deferred; status conditions = minimal reconcile. (3) Lean controller-runtime, growing. (4) First earned capability = own CI as the gate-family (dagmar-bootstrap prepare once-per-workspace + dagmar-gate verify in-loop) implemented as ALWAYS-DAGGER FUNCTIONS (Dagger SDKs cover Go/TS/Python/PHP; no Justfile/just/bun). dagmar-gate is the WRAPPER over manifest-declared checkables (ADR-0003 untouched), NOT 'the checkable'. Hermeticity carve-out: dagmar-gate is a named Dagger fn != raw container tool (ADR-0011 §2), residual = ADR-0011 §3 accepted; gate body project-declared/gate-reviewed, in-loop pinned ref. REASSIGNS ADR-0009 §2 (Justfile targets -> Dagger fns; just not used; conformance strengthens to Project-is-a-Dagger-module). (5) Trajectory: cognition-before-autonomy (P0 control-plane glue -> P1 CI -> P2 cognition Loop+workspace then os-eco -> P3 autonomy triggers+merge-policy then housekeeping; productionization alongside).

name: dagmar self-bootstrap trajectory (phases)
description: dagmar's self-bootstrap order (ADR-0012): Phase 0 control-plane glue (CRD types api/v1alpha1/ + lean controller-runtime reconciler in cmd/dagmar-controller/, on a local kind cluster; dispatch vertical WITHOUT LLM proves CRD->Controller->kube-pod://; agent-pod image + module ref are Phase-0 reads; status conditions are the minimal reconcile) -> Phase 1 own CI (dagmar-bootstrap + dagmar-gate as ALWAYS-DAGGER functions, wired into GitHub Actions via dagger-for-github; reused in-loop) -> Phase 2 cognition (dag.LLM().Loop() wrapping + workspace/repo model FIRST, then os-eco adapter impls sd/ml/cn; coder self-verifies via dagmar-gate) -> Phase 3 autonomy (trigger model + merge-policy = reactive; then proactive housekeeping). Productionization (kind->real cluster, state/persistence, RBAC/Helm) runs alongside. Cognition BEFORE autonomy (ADR-0006: autonomy earned). Conformance: a Project is a Dagger module exposing dagmar-bootstrap + dagmar-gate (always-Dagger; no Justfile). dagmar-gate = wrapper over manifest checkables (ADR-0003), not the checkable itself. See docs/adr/0012-self-bootstrap-trajectory.md.

name: dagmar controller scaffold (root module)
description: The Kubernetes control plane lives in the ROOT module github.com/denkhaus/dagmar (distinct from the .dagger/ execution module). Layout: api/v1alpha1/{doc,project_types,run_types,groupversion_info}.go + zz_generated.deepcopy.go (Project + Run CRDs, group dagmar.denkhaus.io); internal/controller/run_controller.go (RunReconciler: Run -> resolve Project + singleton engine pod -> provision owned agent pod running 'dagger call <fn>' via kube-pod:// -> mirror pod phase into Run.Status); cmd/dagmar-controller/main.go (lean controller-runtime manager, no webhooks/leader-election, metrics :8080/health :8081); Justfile (manifests/generate/install/run/build/test/vet/fmt/docker-build/deploy); config/{crd,rbac,manager,default,samples}/ kustomize; Dockerfile (multi-stage); PROJECT. Versions: controller-runtime v0.24.x + controller-tools v0.21.x + k8s.io v0.36.x (Go 1.26.1). Two gotchas: (1) doc.go MUST carry '+kubebuilder:object:generate=true' or controller-gen only deepcopies root=true types; (2) controller-gen recipes MUST run with GOWORK=off (its packages.Load trips on the parent /home/denkhaus/dev/gomodules/go.work), though 'go build/test' use the default workspace. Build: 'just build test vet'. Phase 0 of ADR-0012; control-plane internals (concurrency, full reconciliation, webhook admission) deferred to seed dagmar-67bc. CRD types are deliberately NOT shared with .dagger/internal/domain/ (ADR-0012 HOUSE-2).

name: Phase 0 dispatch vertical PROVEN on docker-desktop (ADR-0012 §2)
description: Empirically proven 2026-08-04 (commit d549007): the genuinely-new CRD->Controller->agent-pod->dagger-call->engine-via-kube-pod:// chain, with status mirrored back into the Run CR. On a docker-desktop cluster (substrate deviation from ADR-0012 §1 kind — chosen for k9s inspection; the dispatch path is substrate-agnostic). Recipe: (1) just deploy-engine — cbb8 helm recipe (oci://registry.dagger.io/dagger-helm, image.tag=v0.21.8, privileged, ns dagmar); 2 engine pods (DaemonSet on the workers). (2) just install — applies Project+Run CRDs. (3) just run — controller locally against the kubeconfig. (4) apply-samples — Project(dagmar-own) + Run(smoke-probe-net). (5) controller provisions an OWNED agent pod + a per-namespace dagmar-agent SA + a cross-namespace pods/exec Role/RoleBinding on the engine ns (ensureAgentIdentity). (6) agent pod installs dagger CLI from the GITHUB RELEASE TARBALL (not dl.dagger.io|sh, which 403s in-pod), connects to the engine via _EXPERIMENTAL_DAGGER_RUNNER_HOST=kube-pod://<enginePod>?namespace=dagmar, runs 'dagger call -m github.com/denkhaus/dagmar probe-net'. Engine clones the module server-side, runs probe-net, returns NET_OK. Pod exit 0 -> Run.Status.Phase=Succeeded, Available=True. Gotchas hit+fixed: (a) controller-runtime v0.24 REQUIRES ctrl.SetLogger(zap.New(...)) or it drops logs + spams a priorityqueue stack trace; (b) 'curl dl.dagger.io|sh' 403s from the pod -> use the GitHub release tarball; (c) controller-gen needs GOWORK=off go mod tidy so go.mod is module-mode consistent; (d) moduleRef is load-bearing (empty -> terminal Failed); (e) the module source must be reachable by the UNAUTHENTICATED engine — github.com/denkhaus/dagmar was PRIVATE, flipped public for the smoke; private-module creds = ADR-0007 Phase 2. Relates to [[mx-38d10e]] (trajectory), [[mx-a60620]] (controller scaffold), [[mx-e0cba3]] (kube-pod:// Q3).

name: Phase 1 gate-family: dagmar-bootstrap + dagmar-gate (always-Dagger CI)
description: Phase 1 (ADR-0012 §4, commit ca26df7): dagmar's own CI as always-Dagger functions. dagmar-gate (DagmarGate -> workflows.Gate) reads .dagmar/project.yaml (ADR-0003 manifest) and runs each declared checkable in a golang:1.26 container (mount /src, ReturnTypeAny + DAGMAR_EXIT=$? marker to capture failing output); aborts on first non-zero with the step output. dagmar-bootstrap (DagmarBootstrap -> workflows.Bootstrap) = prepare: go mod download per manifest workdir (HOUSE-5). Method names DagmarGate/DagmarBootstrap expose as dagger functions dagmar-gate/dagmar-bootstrap (the ADR-0009 conformance names; kebab-cased by the Go SDK). Manifest schema: checkables list of {name, workdir, command, env?}. config/manifest.go = pure types + ParseManifest (gopkg.in/yaml.v3), Dagger-free. Reused in CI (GitHub Actions dagger/dagger-for-github@v8.4.1: 'dagger call dagmar-gate --source .') AND later in-loop (Phase 2 coder self-verify). PREREQUISITE FIX: the .dagger generated files (dagger.gen.go, internal/dagger/) are now COMMITTED, not gitignored — the prior .gitignore contradicted the .gitattributes (linguist-generated) + Dagger 'commit the generated files' guidance; a fresh CI checkout lacked them so the .dagger checkable's go build failed. Regenerate via 'dagger develop', commit the result. Verified: 'dagger call dagmar-gate --source .' -> all checkables passed; negative test -> checkable FAILED (exit 1) with output. Relates to [[mx-e47932]] (trajectory), [[mx-97c06e]] (skeleton).

title: ADR-0013: Kubernetes control-plane design (topology, reconciliation, dispatch)
rationale: Decided via grilling dagmar-67bc, revised after review-15 (94a5103). 12 decisions: topology (one manager, one controller per active CRD; no worker pool; no webhooks yet); reconciliation (owner-ref pod watch, Project identity finalizer w/ retained engine-side cache-vol, metav1.Condition); dispatch (per-TASK lineage serialization — corrected from Project per review-15 GAP-1, since Workspaces are per-Run isolated; parallel across Tasks/Projects; lineage on Runs via spec.taskRef + stale-pointer recovery); provisioning (moduleRef on Project.spec, agent-image platform default + Agent.spec optional override, per-Project scoped engine-git-creds with ADR-0007 consistency conditional on spike); state (hybrid CRs + object-storage; os-eco as manifest-declared tool-ports; hermeticity = tool-surface per ADR-0011, NOT network air-gap). Two spikes filed: dagmar-2c68 (engine-git-creds), dagmar-e8f3 (os-eco wrapping).

name: Dagger private-module auth: git-credential PAT (#8805)
description: How dagmar's singleton Dagger engine authenticates PRIVATE module sources. TWO distinct paths: (A) MODULE-SOURCE LOADING (`dagger call -m github.com/owner/repo`) — engine queries the CLIENT pod's `git credential fill` for the host, receives the PAT, injects it back into that session as a Dagger secret, fetches transiently. Shipped v0.14.0 (PR #8805 'PAT support -- private git on http/https'; closes dagger/dagger#6113, #7990); present in our v0.21.8. For a headless agent pod: gitconfig + non-interactive credential helper emitting a PAT from an env var. (B) IN-FUNCTION git (`dag.Git(url, GitOpts{HTTPAuthToken: *Secret})`) — auth via a graph `*Secret` (`dag.SetSecret`); DOES NOT apply to -m module loading. KEY INVARIANTS: `setSecret`/secrets are per-session/per-client, isolated across client connections (no cross-Project leakage); the engine holds NO standing credential — each client session brings its own PAT. This is why ADR-0013 D10's invariant holds and ADR-0007 consistency is satisfied (per-Project K8s Secret -> projected into that Project's agent pod -> consumed transiently in-session). Resolves spike dagmar-2c68; see ADR-0013 §4 D10.

name: Private module dispatch via git-credential helper (empirically confirmed)
description: EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED 2026-08-05 on the docker-desktop kind cluster (commit 80a0bba, Run smoke-probe-net reached Succeeded in ~24s, ProbeNet verdict NET_OK). The git-credential fill callback (PR 8805) fires cleanly over kube-pod:// against a remote singleton engine — the spike dagmar-2c68 one runtime uncertainty is resolved. RECIPE (controller agentPodFor, internal/controller/run_controller.go): when Project.Spec.GitCredentialsRef is set, project DAGMAR_GIT_PAT via an env secretKeyRef (Secret in the Run namespace, key defaults to token) and install git plus a global credential.helper that echoes username=dagmar and password=the DAGMAR_GIT_PAT env var (single-quoted in the shell so it expands only at fill time), before the dagger call -m ref. The PAT flows pod-env to credential-helper to engine session-secret; the controller NEVER reads the value — it validates Secret existence only (terminal GitCredentialsSecretNotFound if missing). Local Secret creation without leaking the PAT: pipe gopass show -o through tr -d newline into kubectl create secret with from-file token stdin. GOTCHA: a stale Run+pod from the public-repo era survives the private flip — delete and recreate to exercise new controller code. Relates to the mechanism reference and ADR-0013 section 4 D10.

name: dagmar local-dev environment (cluster + gopass + recipes)
description: How to run dagmar locally for dev/smoke. CLUSTER: a kind cluster on docker-desktop (kubectl context: docker-desktop; nodes desktop-control-plane/desktop-worker/desktop-worker2) is kept ALWAYS RUNNING — do not create or tear it down per session. ENGINE: the singleton Dagger engine is a privileged DaemonSet named dagger-dagger-helm-engine (label name=dagger-dagger-helm-engine) in namespace dagmar, helm-installed via oci registry.dagger.io/dagger-helm image.tag v0.21.8; it PERSISTS across sessions, so just deploy-engine is rarely needed. PRIVATE-MODULE PAT: lives in gopass at key dev/dagmar/github_token (fine-grained, contents read on github.com/denkhaus/dagmar); create the cluster Secret leak-free with just git-creds (pipes gopass show -o through tr -d newline into kubectl create secret --from-file token stdin). SMOKE FLOW: just install (CRDs), just git-creds (Secret), just run (controller out-of-cluster, run in background), just apply-samples (Project dagmar-own + Run smoke-probe-net); then kubectl get run smoke-probe-net -w until Succeeded, kubectl logs smoke-probe-net-agent shows ProbeNet NET_OK. GOTCHA: a stale Run+pod from a prior era survives reconciler restarts — delete and recreate to exercise new controller code. See ADR-0013 section 4 D10 and the empirically-confirmed pattern.

title: ADR-0014: Platform/project scope separation (gate-family module boundary)
rationale: Decided via grilling dagmar-b8c2 (2026-08-05). The .dagger module conflated platform-scope (Up/DeployEngine/Probe*/Sandbox) and project-scope (dagmar-bootstrap/dagmar-gate) code; the platform shortcircuited the abstraction a normal project uses (call the project module by ref). Six decisions: (Q1) MODULE boundary, not code boundary -- only a module boundary makes the project module addressable via -m ref and the shortcuit structurally impossible; (Q2) assignment -- Up/DeployEngine/Probe*/Sandbox = platform, dagmar-bootstrap/dagmar-gate + workflows.Bootstrap/Gate = project, Sandbox is the agent exec context; (Q3) paths -- .dagger = platform module (keeps name), .dagmar = project module (NEW, holds moved gate/bootstrap code + existing manifest), local ref -m .dagmar; (Q4/D2) invocation = direct + convention, no central wrapper now, conformance by ADR+naming; (Q5/D3) dogfood = LOCAL ref now, module boundary enforces the ref call, published/subpath-ref deferred; (Q6/D4) toolchain rollout = project-specific, no platform default, shared helper only at multi-project reuse. Consequence: the held gate-centralization restructure (mise bootstrap + secrets checkable) is re-homed from .dagger/internal/workflows/ to .dagmar/, CI/lefthook becomes -m .dagmar call dagmar-gate. Builds on ADR-0010 + ADR-0009 section 2 + ADR-0012 section 4.

content: The dagmar-review omnigent agent (.omnigent/agent-configs/config.yaml) MUST stay spawn:false. With spawn:true it delegated each review to a nested general-purpose sub-agent that produced no output, so the report never landed -- the double-delegation stall that bit reviews 15 and 17 (parent completed, orphan child kept running, docs/review/NN-*.md never written, watcher timed out). An advice-only reviewer (read corpus + write one report, 200k context) has no legitimate need to spawn sub-agents. Fixed 2026-08-05 commit c792362; validated by review-17b (sound 123-line review on first run). Generalizes: single-purpose advice/report agents default spawn:false unless delegation is a real requirement.
